method: Same harness, data, versions, isolated release builds, 4,000,000 rows, batch size 8192, null every 17th value, 256 groups. 3 processes per engine/worker setting, 2 warmups and 10 measurements per case. Alternating engine order. Median of process medians; ranges are not confidence intervals.
correctness: Every row, value, null and schema checked before timing in all 12 processes. Row count checked after every timed run. Additional generated-reduction tests cover sliced null bitmaps, arbitrary payloads underneath nulls, tails, empty input, wrapping sums and repeated state updates. Group-cache tests cover collisions, nulls and full-width keys.
timing: Execution excludes graph construction and JIT; both are separately timed. It includes initialization, scheduling, complete output collection and cleanup. This is resident input, not I/O. Scan only transfers batch ownership. It is a whole-branch comparison, not isolated attribution to codegen.
result: All 12 execution medians are lower than main. Single-worker scan has overlapping process ranges and only a small improvement. Compile-inclusive latency is not faster for every workload; global aggregation still has about 1 ms preparation cost.
threading: Both use 1/4 pipeline workers and Tokio threads. Current uses a Rayon pool of the same size for parallel CPU work; one-worker work runs inline. Immediately ready batches are dispatched in bounded chunks, retaining pending reads.
optimizations: Borrow numeric Arrow buffers and bitmaps; direct 64-bit output buffers
Immediate literals, visible source common subexpressions and loop-invariant descriptors
Generated integer SUM/COUNT updates; vector global reductions with sparse/dense null handling
Bounded collision-checked word-key cache; reusable scratch for other keys
Identity batch transfer, inline single-worker execution and eager/coalesced parallel CPU dispatch

inkfuse.reason: Native macOS build needs more than compiler configuration changes: Linux eventfd, pidfd_open, CPU affinity, linker/archive commands and Darwin uint64_t/size_t ABI differences. No comparable InkFuse timing is claimed. Paper uses an i9-10900 on Linux with TPC-H data, not this M4 Pro harness.
